name: $k$-Block Littlestone Dimension of Singletons
proof: For every fixed $k>2$, a depth-one tree is allowed as a truncated block. It is shattered when $n\ge2$, since any coordinate has both labels. Every root has a singleton positive branch, ruling out complete depth two regardless of block constraints. Thus the value is one for $n\ge2$. At $n=1$, no coordinate splits the class and the value is zero. This agrees with Proposition \ref{prop:block-littlestone-sandwich}.
